Oh! Great: Oh! great is known for his dynamic, detailed art in the martial arts series Tenjho Tenge and the inline-skating action hit Air Gear, and he draws the manga of Nisio Isin's Bakemonogatari.
Yomu Mishima: Yomu Mishima writes the comedic fantasy light novels Trapped in a Dating Sim: The World of Otome Games Is Tough for Mobs and I'm the Evil Lord of an Intergalactic Empire!.
Hirohiko Araki: Hirohiko Araki created JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, the stylish, wildly inventive saga running since 1987, along with spin-offs like Thus Spoke Rohan Kishibe and Rohan at the Louvre.
Yuya Aoki: Yuya Aoki wrote GetBackers, the action series about two retrieval agents drawn by Rando Ayamine, and the supernatural adventure Psycho Busters.
Hiro Ainana: Hiro Ainana writes Death March to the Parallel World Rhapsody, the easygoing isekai about a programmer who wakes up overpowered in a fantasy world.
Adachitoka: Adachitoka is the two-woman team behind Noragami: Stray God, the stylish story of a homeless god who takes odd jobs for five yen.
Koge-Donbo: Koge-Donbo creates cute, sparkly comedies like Pita-Ten, Kamichama Karin and Kon Kon Kokon, and designed the characters of Di Gi Charat.
Makoto Tateno: Makoto Tateno is known for boys' love manga such as Yellow, Ka Shin Fu and Hate to Love You, as well as Happy Boys and King of Cards.
Suu Morishita: Suu Morishita is the two-person team behind the gentle romances A Sign of Affection, Shortcake Cake and Like a Butterfly.
Dall-Young Lim: Dall-Young Lim is a Korean writer known for the action series Freezing, Black God and Unbalance x Unbalance.
Kennoji: Kennoji writes popular light novels including Hazure Skill: The Guild Member with a Worthless Skill Is Actually a Legendary Assassin, The Girl I Saved on the Train Turned Out to Be My Childhood Friend and Drugstore in Another World.
Q Hayashida: Q Hayashida created the grimy, darkly funny fantasy Dorohedoro and the cosmic horror-comedy Dai Dark.
Yukito Kishiro: Yukito Kishiro created Battle Angel Alita (Gunnm), the cyberpunk classic about a cyborg girl, and its sequels Last Order and Mars Chronicle.
Rikdo Koshi: Rikdo Koshi created Excel Saga, the chaotic parody comedy about a hyperactive agent trying to conquer the city.
Soichiro Yamamoto: Soichiro Yamamoto creates sweet, playful rom-coms: Teasing Master Takagi-san and When Will Ayumu Make His Move?.
LINK: LINK writes World's End Harem, the sci-fi drama drawn by Kotaro Shono, and its fantasy spin-off World's End Harem: Fantasia.
Mineko Ohkami: Mineko Ohkami created Dragon Knights, the long-running fantasy adventure about three knights serving the Dragon Lord.
OKAYADO: OKAYADO created the monster-girl comedy Monster Musume: Everyday Life with Monster Girls and the action series 12 Beast.
Yuriko Nishiyama: Yuriko Nishiyama is known for the street-basketball manga Harlem Beat and its sequel Rebound, plus the music story Dragon Voice.
Kazuya Minekura: Kazuya Minekura created Saiyuki, the stylish action retelling of Journey to the West, along with Wild Adapter and Bus Gamer.
Ken Wakui: Ken Wakui created Tokyo Revengers, the time-travel delinquent drama, and the earlier Shinjuku Swan.
Hisaya Nakajo: Hisaya Nakajo created Hana-Kimi, the hit shojo comedy about a girl who disguises herself to attend an all-boys school, and the figure-skating story Sugar Princess.
Jinsei Kataoka and Kazuma Kondou: Jinsei Kataoka and Kazuma Kondou are the team behind the prison survival thriller Deadman Wonderland, the Eureka Seven manga and Smokin' Parade.
Daisuke Ashihara: Daisuke Ashihara created World Trigger, the strategic sci-fi action series about agents defending Earth from invaders called Neighbors.
Miki Aihara: Miki Aihara creates dramatic shojo romances including Hot Gimmick, Honey Hunt and Tokyo Boys & Girls.
Yeo Beop-Ryong: Yeo Beop-Ryong is a Korean writer best known for the martial arts fantasy Chronicles of the Cursed Sword, drawn by Park Hui-Jin.
Satoru Yamaguchi: Satoru Yamaguchi writes My Next Life as a Villainess: All Routes Lead to Doom!, the comedy about a girl reborn as an otome-game villainess.
Naoe: Naoe created the survival-game action comedy Aoharu x Machinegun and the sci-fi series Tokyo Aliens.
You Higuri: You Higuri is known for lush, gothic manga like Cantarella, Seimaden and Gorgeous Carat, and drew the Gakuen Heaven manga.
Osamu Nishi: Osamu Nishi created Welcome to Demon School! Iruma-kun, the funny, big-hearted story of a human boy at a school for demons.
Ryu Fujisaki: Ryu Fujisaki created Hoshin Engi, the playful take on Chinese myth, and the fantasy WaqWaq.
Yun Kouga: Yun Kouga created Loveless, Gestalt and Earthian, and wrote Akuma no Riddle: Riddle Story of Devil.
Yoshifumi Tozuka: Yoshifumi Tozuka created Undead Unluck, the wild action series about an immortal man and a girl whose touch brings bad luck.
Keiichi Arawi: Keiichi Arawi creates surreal everyday comedies: Nichijou: My Ordinary Life and City.
Norihiro Yagi: Norihiro Yagi created Claymore, the dark fantasy about half-human warriors who hunt monsters, and the delinquent comedy Angel Densetsu.
Keiichi Sigsawa: Keiichi Sigsawa writes Kino's Journey: The Beautiful World, the thoughtful travel novels, and Sword Art Online Alternative: Gun Gale Online.
Natsu Hyuuga: Natsu Hyuuga writes The Apothecary Diaries, the hit mystery about a sharp young apothecary solving puzzles in an imperial palace.
Akira Himekawa: Akira Himekawa is the two-woman team behind the Legend of Zelda manga, adapting games like Ocarina of Time, Majora's Mask, The Minish Cap and Twilight Princess.
Matsuri Akino: Matsuri Akino created Pet Shop of Horrors, the eerie tales of a mysterious Chinatown pet shop, and its sequel Pet Shop of Horrors: Tokyo.
Chika Shiomi: Chika Shiomi creates supernatural shojo like Yurara, Rasetsu, Night of the Beasts and Yukarism.
Katsu Aki: Katsu Aki drew the manga of The Vision of Escaflowne, created Psychic Academy, and is known for the long-running couples' manga Futari Ecchi (Manga Sutra).
Rinko Ueda: Rinko Ueda created the ninja romance Tail of the Moon and the Meiji-era shojo Stepping on Roses.
Sorata Akizuki: Sorata Akizuki created Snow White with the Red Hair, the gentle fantasy romance about an herbalist and a prince.
Yoshimurakana: Yoshimurakana created Murcielago, the over-the-top action series about a mass murderer turned police assassin.
Makoto Fukami: Makoto Fukami is a screenwriter and author who co-wrote Psycho-Pass, wrote Magical Girl Spec-Ops Asuka and the novel Berserk: The Flame Dragon Knight.
Inio Asano: Inio Asano creates raw, honest stories about modern life, including Goodnight Punpun, Solanin, A Girl on the Shore and Dead Dead Demon's Dededede Destruction.
Nico Tanigawa: Nico Tanigawa (a two-person team) created No Matter How I Look at It, It's You Guys' Fault I'm Not Popular! (WataMote), the cringe comedy about a socially awkward girl.
Toshio Satou: Toshio Satou writes Suppose a Kid from the Last Dungeon Boonies Moved to a Starter Town, the comedy about a boy who has no idea how strong he is.
Hitsuji Gondaira: Hitsuji Gondaira created the spy family action comedy Mission: Yozakura Family and drew the yuri ghost story Kindred Spirits on the Roof.
Zappon: Zappon writes Banished from the Hero's Party, I Decided to Live a Quiet Life in the Countryside, the cozy fantasy about a knight who opens an apothecary.
Masami Kurumada: Masami Kurumada created Saint Seiya (Knights of the Zodiac), the legendary series of armored warriors, plus B't X and the boxing classic Ring ni Kakero.
Maki Murakami: Maki Murakami created Gravitation, the boys' love comedy about a pop singer and a novelist, along with Gamerz Heaven and Kanpai!.
Yu Okano: Yu Okano writes The Unwanted Undead Adventurer, about a long-time adventurer who comes back as a skeleton and keeps climbing.
Masami Tsuda: Masami Tsuda created Kare Kano (His and Her Circumstances), the school romance about two students who seem perfect but are hiding their real selves.
Kiyohiko Azuma: Kiyohiko Azuma created the cheerful comedies Yotsuba&! and Azumanga Daioh.
Takashi Hashiguchi: Takashi Hashiguchi created Yakitate!! Japan, the over-the-top baking comedy about a boy aiming to make Japan's national bread.
Hitoshi Okuda: Hitoshi Okuda wrote and drew the long-running No Need for Tenchi! manga and The All-New Tenchi Muyo!.
Akihisa Ikeda: Akihisa Ikeda created Rosario + Vampire, the action comedy about a human boy at a school for monsters, and its sequel Season II.
Miwa Ueda: Miwa Ueda created the hit shojo drama Peach Girl, its spin-offs, and Papillon.
Eiji Masuda: Eiji Masuda created My Monster Secret, the rom-com about a boy who can't keep a secret and the vampire girl he falls for.
Sakon Kaidou: Sakon Kaidou writes Infinite Dendrogram, the light novel about a VR game so real its world feels alive.
Kazuo Koike: Kazuo Koike (1936-2019) wrote the classic samurai saga Lone Wolf and Cub, plus Lady Snowblood and Crying Freeman.
Yuhki Kamatani: Yuhki Kamatani created the ninja fantasy Nabari no Ou and the moving Our Dreams at Dusk.
Hiroshi Shiibashi: Hiroshi Shiibashi created Nura: Rise of the Yokai Clan, about a boy who is heir to a powerful yokai clan.
Kazuki Funatsu: Kazuki Funatsu created the romantic comedy Sundome and the yokai comedy Yokai Girls.
Chie Shinohara: Chie Shinohara created Red River, the epic historical romance about a girl pulled back in time to the Hittite Empire.
Ayuko Hatta: Ayuko Hatta created Wolf Girl and Black Prince, the hit shojo rom-com, and Ima Koi: Now I'm in Love.
Kaoru Shinozaki: Kaoru Shinozaki writes Failure Frame, the dark revenge isekai about a boy cast aside with a skill everyone thinks is useless.
Yasuo Ohtagaki: Yasuo Ohtagaki created Mobile Suit Gundam Thunderbolt, the gritty, jazz-filled war story set in the Gundam universe.
Koushi Tachibana: Koushi Tachibana writes the light novels Date A Live and King's Proposal.
HERO: HERO created the original webcomic of Horimiya, the sweet high school romance, and Ako and Bambi.
Yoshiki Tanaka: Yoshiki Tanaka is the novelist behind the space opera Legend of the Galactic Heroes and the fantasy epic The Heroic Legend of Arslan.
Yayoi Ogawa: Yayoi Ogawa created Tramps Like Us, the romance about a career woman who takes in a young man as her pet, and the figure-skating story Knight of the Ice.
Naoshi Komi: Naoshi Komi created Nisekoi: False Love, the hit romantic comedy about two teens forced to fake a relationship.
Junji Ito: Junji Ito is the master of horror manga, known for Uzumaki, Gyo, Tomie and many chilling short story collections.
Hikaru Miyoshi: Hikaru Miyoshi draws Moriarty the Patriot, the Sherlock Holmes reimagining written by Ryosuke Takeuchi, and drew the Psycho-Pass manga.
Ennki Hakari: Ennki Hakari writes Skeleton Knight in Another World, about a gamer stuck in a fantasy world as his armored skeleton character.
Tsutomu Sato: Tsutomu Sato writes The Irregular at Magic High School, the sci-fi magic series, and its many spin-offs.
In-Soo Ra: In-Soo Ra is a Korean writer best known for King of Hell, the action series drawn by Jae-Hwan Kim.
Shinobu Gotoh: Shinobu Gotoh is a boys' love novelist known for the long-running Takumi-kun series and Passion.
Eiichi Shimizu: Eiichi Shimizu co-creates the Ultraman manga with Tomohiro Shimoguchi, a modern continuation of the classic tokusatsu hero.
Akira Hiramoto: Akira Hiramoto created the outrageous comedy Prison School and Raw Hero.
Mine Yoshizaki: Mine Yoshizaki created Sgt. Frog (Keroro Gunso), the comedy about a frog-like alien invader who would rather build Gundam models.
Yuto Suzuki: Yuto Suzuki created Sakamoto Days, the action comedy about a legendary hitman who retires to run a convenience store.
Yuji Shiozaki: Yuji Shiozaki created Battle Vixens (Ikki Tousen), the martial arts action series inspired by Romance of the Three Kingdoms.
Kenji Inoue: Kenji Inoue writes Grand Blue Dreaming, the hilarious college diving comedy drawn by Kimitake Yoshioka, and created Baka and Test.
Junya Inoue: Junya Inoue created Btooom!, the survival thriller about players trapped on an island playing a real-life bombing game.
Tadahiro Miura: Tadahiro Miura created Yuuna and the Haunted Hot Springs, the comedy about a boy who lives with a ghost girl at a hot spring inn.
Takahiro: Takahiro wrote Akame ga Kill! and writes Chained Soldier and Hinowa ga Crush!.
Daisuke Higuchi: Daisuke Higuchi created Whistle!, the soccer manga about a small boy with big determination.
Yu Shimizu: Yu Shimizu writes The Demon Sword Master of Excalibur Academy, about a demon lord reborn as a boy at a magic academy.
Satoru Nii: Satoru Nii created Wind Breaker, the delinquent action series about a high school gang that protects its town.
Woo: Woo (Lee Kang-Woo) is the Korean artist behind Rebirth, the dark action manhwa about a vampire seeking revenge.
Hideyuki Kikuchi: Hideyuki Kikuchi is the horror novelist behind Vampire Hunter D, the gothic sci-fi saga of a half-vampire hunter, along with Yashakiden and Taimashin.
Ray Omishi: Ray Omishi wrote Sorcerer Hunters, the fantasy action comedy drawn by Satoshi Shiki.
Chugong: Chugong is the Korean web novelist behind Solo Leveling, the hit story of a weak hunter who becomes the strongest of all.
Sankichi Hinodeya: Sankichi Hinodeya draws the colorful Splatoon manga, based on Nintendo's ink-shooting games, including Splatoon 3: Splatlands.
Noriyuki Konishi: Noriyuki Konishi draws the Yo-kai Watch manga, about a boy who can see and befriend mischievous yokai.
Jougi Shiraishi: Jougi Shiraishi writes Wandering Witch: The Journey of Elaina, about a young witch traveling from one strange land to the next.
Strike Tanaka: Strike Tanaka created Servamp, the supernatural action series about a boy who forms a contract with a lazy vampire who turns into a cat.
Yuuki Iinuma: Yuuki Iinuma created Itsuwaribito, the adventure about a boy who uses lies to help people.
Hinako Takanaga: Hinako Takanaga is known for boys' love manga such as Challengers, Little Butterfly, Croquis, Liberty Liberty! and The Tyrant Falls in Love.
Yoko Nogiri: Yoko Nogiri creates sweet shojo romances like That Wolf-Boy Is Mine!, Love in Focus and Those Not-So-Sweet Boys.
Ryoko Fukuyama: Ryoko Fukuyama created the music romance Anonymous Noise and the sci-fi shojo Nosatsu Junkie.
Yasunori Mitsunaga: Yasunori Mitsunaga created the monster-filled action comedy Princess Resurrection.
Katarina: Katarina writes Shangri-La Frontier, the action story about a gamer who loves bad games tackling a masterpiece VR world.
Yu Sasuga: Yu Sasuga wrote Terra Formars, the sci-fi action series about humans battling giant mutant cockroaches on Mars.
Taro Hitsuji: Taro Hitsuji writes Akashic Records of Bastard Magic Instructor and Last Round Arthurs.
Isshiki Ichika: Isshiki Ichika writes Berserk of Gluttony, the dark fantasy about a boy whose hunger skill lets him devour the powers of those he defeats.
Motoo Nakanishi: Motoo Nakanishi writes Sword of the Demon Hunter: Kijin Gentosho, the centuries-spanning saga of a swordsman hunting demons.
Abi Umeda: Abi Umeda created Children of the Whales, the haunting fantasy about people living on a drifting island in a sea of sand.
Kei Sanbe: Kei Sanbe is best known for the time-travel thriller Erased, and also created The 13th Footprint, Kamiyadori and For the Kid I Saw in My Dreams.
Hideaki Sorachi: Hideaki Sorachi created Gintama, the samurai sci-fi comedy famous for its parodies and surprisingly emotional arcs.
Riku Misora: Riku Misora writes High School Prodigies Have It Easy Even in Another World!, about seven gifted teens who reshape a fantasy kingdom.
Ryo Hanada: Ryo Hanada created Devils' Line, the romance and action series about a half-vampire police officer.
Ao Jyumonji: Ao Jyumonji writes Grimgar of Fantasy and Ash, the grounded fantasy about strangers who wake up in a world with no memory and must survive.
Banri Hidaka: Banri Hidaka created the shojo romances V.B. Rose and I Hate You More Than Anyone!.
Ai Morinaga: Ai Morinaga creates goofy romantic comedies like My Heavenly Hockey Club, Your and My Secret and Duck Prince.
